name: Half Guard Bottom Escape
description: Escape from bottom half guard by winning the underhook, creating a frame, and regaining guard or standing up.
shortInstruction: Win the underhook, bring the outside knee across the opponent's back, and drive to dogfight or recover butterfly guard.
summary: Half guard bottom escape uses the underhook and outside knee position to create a dogfight entry, from which you can wrestle up, sweep, or recover full guard. The system rewards hip mobility and head position over upper-body strength.
whyItWorks: The underhook removes the opponent's crossface threat and gives you control of their upper body posture
The outside knee across the back creates a structural wedge that prevents them from flattening you back down
The dogfight position gives you three branches: single leg (wrestle up), knee tap (sweep), or re-guard (recover butterfly)
Winning the head position (forehead to their jaw) prevents them from crushing you with shoulder pressure
commonMistakes: Fighting for the underhook from a flat back instead of turning to the side first
Letting the opponent crossface while reaching for the underhook — this exposes the neck
Pulling the underhook arm out instead of driving the elbow upward into their armpit
Staying in dogfight too long without committing to a branch — the opponent will eventually flatten you
safetySummary: Half guard is the most common place to injure fingers and toes — keep digits safe when gripping pants or inserting hooks
If the opponent has a strong crossface, protect your neck by turning your head toward the mat before reaching for the underhook
Do not force the dogfight if your knee is trapped — this can stress the MCL

systemLogic.corePrinciple: The half guard bottom escape has three sequential steps: turn to side → win underhook → insert outside knee across back

decisionTree.action: If Step 1, Turn to side: before reaching for anything, turn onto your side facing the opponent. This aligns your skeleton for frame and prevents them from flattening you
If Step 2, Win underhook: pummel your near arm deep into their armpit with the elbow driving up. Your head must be either inside (forehead to jaw) or outside (cheek to their shoulder)

decisionTree.condition: Step 3, Outside knee: bring your outside knee across their lower back and post your foot. This creates the dog

decisionTree.action: From dogfight, you have three branches: single leg (they post far hand), knee tap (they post close), or re-guard (they drive into you)

moneyDetails: Half guard bottom is one of the most common positions in BJJ — a reliable escape here dramatically improves your overall game
A successful half guard escape leads directly to a dominant top position (side control or mount via the pass)
Escaping half guard to wrestle-up scores a takedown in competition (2 points) and establishes top control
fixItFast: If they smash you flat before you get the underhook: go to deep half guard and sweep them over the trapped leg
If they crossface you hard: hide your head, go to your side, and use your top arm to frame on their biceps instead of reaching for the underhook
If they knee slide through your half guard: immediately turn into them, trap their passing leg between yours, and re-pummel for the underhook
